It also decreases metoprolol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To minimize this interaction, administer calcium carbonate and metoprolol at least 2 hours apart. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Calcium carbonate and mexiletine: Calcium carbonate increases the levels and effects of mexiletine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. This interaction necessitates caution and close monitoring. Consider separating the administration of these agents. 3. Calcium carbonate and minocycline: Calcium carbonate and minocycline reduce each other’s levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, separate the doses by at least 2 hours. 4. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. To mitigate this interaction, administer the drugs at least 2 hours apart and monitor closely. 6. Calcium carbonate and mycophenolate: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels and effects of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 7. Calcium carbonate and nadolol: Calcium carbonate reduces the effectiveness of nadolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. It also decreases nadolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer the drugs at least 2 hours apart and monitor closely.
